### Problem: Static Range Sum Queries {#sec-pref-p1-a}

::: {.p-statement}
An array of $n$ integers ($1 \le n \le 2\cdot10^5$, each value at most $10^9$) and $q$ queries ($1 \le q \le 2\cdot10^5$). Each query gives $a \le b$, **1-based and inclusive**, and asks for the sum of the values from position $a$ to position $b$. Print one line per query.

Source: [CSES 1646 · Static Range Sum Queries](https://cses.fi/problemset/task/1646){.solved}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
Nothing in the array ever changes, so each query is asking for the difference of two running totals you could have computed once. The only real difficulty is the index convention: the judge's inclusive $[a,b]$ is our half-open $[a-1, b)$, and with $P$ built as in @eq-pref-build the translation is mechanical.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **Brute force.** For each query, loop from $a$ to $b$ adding: $O(n)$ per query, so $O(nq) = 4\cdot10^{10}$ at the limits — a certain timeout against the budget of @sec-arr-cost.
2. **Prefix table.** Build $P$ once in $O(n)$; answer each query as $P[b] - P[a-1]$ in $O(1)$. Total $O(n+q)$.

**Invariant.** $P[i]$ is the sum of the first $i$ cells, so $P[b]-P[a-1]$ is the sum of exactly the cells $a,a+1,\dots,b$ — the two ends that a naive inclusive table would trip over are handled by $P[0]=0$.
:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Per-query loop

::: {.form-next}
Read the query as it is written: add up $a[x-1], \dots, a[y-1]$. Nothing is prepared, so nothing can be stale, and nothing is shared either — a range of length $\ell$ costs $\ell$ additions and then the work is thrown away. This is the version the stress test below keeps as its oracle.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
def static_range_sums_brute(a, queries):
    return [sum(a[x - 1:y]) for x, y in queries]
```

##### C++

```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr);
    int n, q; cin >> n >> q;
    vector<long long> a(n);
    for (auto& x : a) cin >> x;
    while (q--) {
        int l, r; cin >> l >> r;             // 1-based inclusive
        long long tot = 0;
        for (int i = l - 1; i < r; ++i) tot += a[i];
        cout << tot << '\n';
    }
}
```
:::

#### Prefix table

::: {.form-next}
Overlapping ranges share almost all of their terms, and a range sum only ever needs two numbers. Build $P$ once in one forward pass, and every query — of any length — becomes the single subtraction $P[y] - P[x-1]$. The table is the whole change; the query line does not even look like a loop any more.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("range", "table")
    assert str(final) == "[3, 9, 12]"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: arr-static-range-sums
def static_range_sums(a: list[int], queries: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> list[int]:
    """Each query is (x, y), 1-based and inclusive, as CSES states it."""
    p = build_prefix(a)
    return [p[y] - p[x - 1] for x, y in queries]


for _ in range(400):
    a = [random.randint(1, 10**9) for _ in range(random.randint(1, 14))]
    queries = []
    for _ in range(10):
        x = random.randint(1, len(a))
        queries.append((x, random.randint(x, len(a))))
    assert static_range_sums(a, queries) == static_range_sums_brute(a, queries)

assert static_range_sums([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], [(1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 5)]) == [3, 9, 12]
assert static_range_sums([7], [(1, 1)]) == [7]
print("static_range_sums OK")
```

##### C++

```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr);
    int n, q; cin >> n >> q;
    vector<long long> p(n + 1, 0);          // 2e5 * 1e9 needs 64-bit
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        long long x; cin >> x;
        p[i + 1] = p[i] + x;                // eq-pref-build
    }
    while (q--) {
        int a, b; cin >> a >> b;            // 1-based inclusive
        cout << p[b] - p[a - 1] << '\n';    // eq-pref-range
    }
}
```
:::
:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Per-query loop** is $O(nq)$: $4\cdot10^{10}$ additions at the limits of @sec-arr-cost, a certain timeout. **Prefix table** is $O(n + q)$ — one addition per cell to build, three operations per query. **Space** $O(n)$ for the table, the price of $O(1)$ queries and the cheapest trade in the book.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- $a = 1$: the read is $P[0]$, which exists *because* the table has $n+1$ cells. A table built the inclusive way would need a branch here.
- $a = b$: a single cell, $P[a]-P[a-1]$, no special case.
- The whole array: $P[n]-P[0]$, where $P[n]$ is the total — "everything" costs the same as any other query, which is what makes the extra cell worth having.
- Overflow: `long long` for the table **and** for the value you read into, or the accumulation silently wraps (@sec-arr-cost).
:::
